Skala-Podilska Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Skala-Podilska was home to an extraordinary diversity of Hasidic streams — including Vizhnitz, Chortkiv, Ottynia, and Strusiv, among others — supporting ten Hasidic prayer houses at its peak. During the Civil War, the community suffered attacks from Petliura's troops, the Bolsheviks, and the Polish army in succession. During Hungarian and German occupation, local Jews were deported to the Janowska transit camp in Lviv, documented elsewhere in this collection, the Bełżec extermination camp, and the Borschiv ghetto; around 150 survived. This cemetery, marked on a map in the 1978 Yizkor book Sefer Skalah and a memorial tablet dating it to the 1580s, was fenced in 1997, and about 30 recovered gravestones are now stored near its entrance.
